title: Dynamic Creatures Launches First Human Companion Robot Hugo
summary:
A new partnership between former executives from Boston Dynamics and the RAI Institute has resulted in the creation of a machine capable of interpreting human emotion. The robot, named Hugo, utilizes a Vision-Language-Expression (VLE) model to synchronize visual and auditory inputs with physical movement and facial expressions in real time. This technology allows the device to recognize individuals and adjust its behavior based on the social dynamics of a room.

Dynamic Creatures, the company behind Hugo, is the official entertainment and hospitality partner for Boston Dynamics. Co-founders Tim Ermann and Farbod Farshidian bring more than 15 years of experience in robotic mobility and industrial systems to the venture. The startup is developing a wider cast of characters for deployment in theme parks, resorts, and film studios.

selectedTweets.text:
Introducing Hugo: the first human companion robot.

At Boston Dynamics, I was Chief Strategy Officer, bringing robots into the real world.

My co-founder, Farbod Farshidian, led research at the RAI Institute.

Together, 15+ years teaching robots to run, jump, and work.

So we asked: what if robots could connect with people?

Hugo runs on the first Vision-Language-Expression (VLE) model.

He links what he sees and hears to movement, expression, and gesture.

He notices you, reads the room, and reacts in real time.

And he's only the first.

Dynamic Creatures is @BostonDynamics' official entertainment and hospitality partner.

We're building a cast of characters with film studios, resorts, and theme parks.
